title: fix(chartqa): compare explicit percentages in the same units
body:
## Problem

ChartQA's relaxed scorer attempts a one-sided division by 100 whenever either value contains `%`, including when both values explicitly use percentages. Consequently, `1%` and `100%`, or `0.5%` and `50%`, can incorrectly receive full credit despite differing by a factor of 100. This also affects the explicit-final-answer path of the anywhere scorer.

## Change

Apply the existing unit-conversion fallback only when exactly one value contains `%`. Values that both use percentages are compared in the same units using the existing 5% relative tolerance. The historical permissive conversion when only one value contains `%` remains unchanged. Equivalent conditional and generator-expression cleanups address existing whole-file Ruff findings without changing the non-final-answer fallback.

The adapted [Mistral reference scorer](https://github.com/mistralai/mistral-evals/blob/main/eval/metrics.py) contains the same behavior. This correction is therefore recorded as task version 0.1, inherited by chartqa, chartqa_llama, and chartqa_llama_90. The README identifies the scoring difference: affected relaxed/anywhere scores should not be directly compared with version 0.0; exact-match scoring is unchanged.

## Validation

- 59 new tests on the upstream base: 22 failed, 37 passed.
- Fixed tests plus the existing core metrics tests: 67 passed.
- Controls cover reversed and negative factor-of-100 errors, zeros, the relative-tolerance boundary, one-sided percentage conversions, ordinary numeric answers, multiple references, and the original anywhere fallback.
- Native ConfigurableTask instances loaded from all three actual YAML configurations construct generation requests and score in-memory Dataset examples.
- All three resolved configurations report version 0.1.
- Pinned Ruff 0.16.3 lint/format and git diff --check pass.

No model inference, chart images, external benchmark download, or full repository suite was run. The tests establish scoring correctness for these cases, not a change in model capability.
